name: cmd-s-toggles-while-the-sidebar-holds-focus
description:
Cmd+S collapses the sidebar when the sidebar's own WebUI holds first responder. A click on a row is enough to give it focus - which is how a user reaches this state, since the chord is about the surface they just touched.

The control is the hotkey trace: the dispatcher logs which action the chord matched and what became of it, so a chord that reached the window and was declined names its reason, and a chord the harness never delivered leaves no line at all. Both used to read the same - a docked pane and a guess.

actions.note: a real pointer click on the active row (y re-measured after the rows grew to 36px and the pill moved down 16px) - a DOM click over CDP does not move macOS first responder, which the first run proved with responder=BridgedContentView. The active row does not navigate, so the only thing that changes is who holds focus.

assertions.pattern: Atrium: dead-chord probe cmd\+s at prePerform .*responder=RenderWidgetHostViewCocoa.*url=chrome://atrium.top-chrome/sidebar
assertions.label: the-sidebar-held-first-responder
assertions.desc: THE CONTROL: the chord arrived while the sidebar's render widget was first responder, which is the case under test. Without this the scenario grades the working path.

assertions.label: the-chord-fired
assertions.desc: The dispatcher matched the chord and the toggle ran. A declined chord logs its reason on the same prefix instead.
In pixels: the pane collapsed, so the column the rows stood in now shows the page card.
